summary: The @gyomu/ui-core package provides a structured framework for automated form generation and robust UI error management. It leverages domain schemas to derive form metadata and validation logic, ensuring a consistent approach to data entry and user feedback across the application.
responsibilities: Bridge raw data schemas with UI rendering requirements through domain-specific metadata.
Orchestrate the automated generation and state initialization of dynamic forms.
Enforce schema-based validation for individual form fields and aggregate structures.
Standardize UI-level error reporting, categorization, and recovery workflows.
Provide extensible mappings between widget types and their corresponding reactive components.

capabilities.name: Automated Form Generation
capabilities.description: Constructs UI form configurations and initial data states directly from structural data schemas.

capabilities.name: Schema-Driven Validation
capabilities.description: Validates user inputs against predefined CRUD schema constraints to maintain data integrity within forms.

capabilities.name: UI Error Orchestration
capabilities.description: Provides a consistent mechanism to categorize, display, and handle UI-related errors with support for custom retry behaviors.

capabilities.name: Component Rendering Infrastructure
capabilities.description: Enables the registration and association of custom React components with form field types via a centralized renderer registry.

designDecisions: Schema-First: Decouples UI representation from raw data models by treating schemas as the primary source of truth for form generation.
Compositional DSL: Uses specific metadata structures to transform domain schemas into actionable form field definitions.
Strategy-Based Error Handling: Utilizes a registry map to decouple the triggering of errors from the execution of specific recovery or feedback strategies.
Functional Core: Employs functional validation and state building to ensure predictability in form logic.
usageGuidance: Use the DSL module to define metadata for complex forms, ensuring that your data schemas are correctly annotated for UI generation.
Register custom components in the RendererMap to extend the form engine's capability for rendering specialized input types.
Implement consistent error handling by utilizing the UiErrorHandlerMap, ensuring all UI exceptions are caught and processed through the central error engine.
Leverage the provided validation helpers to ensure data integrity before submission, keeping validation logic synchronized with the underlying CRUD schema.
